backup.title: Backups
backup.tip.when: How often to back up and what to put in the archive. The panel does it while it is running.
backup.tip.auto: Back up on schedule while the panel runs. Off — backups only when you press the button.
backup.tip.engine: Put the DSH engine and Node into the archive: then it unpacks on a clean machine without the internet. The archive becomes heavy — hundreds of megabytes.
backup.tip.sessions: Include the session history and attachments. Without it the archive holds only settings, the model key, skills and profiles.
backup.tip.keep: How many recent backups to keep in the folder. Older ones the panel deletes itself.
backup.tip.folder: Where the archives go. By default Documents\DeepSeekHarness-Backups, so a backup is easy to carry on a flash drive.
backup.tip.keys: Pack private keys and certificates (for example %USERPROFILE%\.ssh) into the archive. Off by default: such an archive becomes a secret.
backup.tip.list: Backups already made, newest first. Double-click a row to verify the archive.
backup.tip.check: Verify the selected backup: does its inventory read and do the checksums match.
backup.tip.delete: Delete the selected archive from the backup folder.
backup.tip.refresh: Re-read the backup folder: archives may have appeared or gone outside the panel.
backup.tip.create: Make a backup right now instead of waiting for the schedule.
backup.tip.restore: Bring data back from an archive: pick a backup (from the list or a file), see what is inside and tick what to restore. Before restoring, the panel makes a copy of the current state.
backup.tip.save: Save the settings of this window. The archives themselves do not change.
backup.tip.close: Close the window without changing anything.

readme.title: DSH Panel backup
readme.kindFull: full (with the DSH engine and Node)
readme.item.manifest: manifest.json — inventory: versions, paths, file list with checksums;
readme.item.dshHome: dsh-home/     — DSH data: settings, model key, skills, profiles;
readme.item.engine: engine/       — the DSH engine (@deepseek-ai/dsh) and Node itself.
readme.item.installer: installer/    — the panel installer: use it to install the panel on a clean machine.
readme.item.keys: keys/         — keys and certificates (the machine owner turned on packing them).
readme.howTitle: How to restore on a clean machine:
readme.step1: 1) install the panel: the file installer\dsh-panel-setup.exe from this archive;
readme.step2: 2) in the panel open “Backups” → “Restore from a backup…” and point it at this archive;
readme.step3: 3) tick DSH data, panel settings and the engine — the panel lays everything out itself,
readme.step3b: including Node, if the machine has none (no internet needed);
readme.step4: 4) keys from keys/ come back only with a separate checkbox.
readme.manual: If the archive is not at hand, the same can be done by hand:
readme.manualRest: engine/ → global npm packages and the Node folder, keys/ → wherever they came from.
readme.warn1: WARNING: if the archive has a keys/ directory, it holds private keys.
readme.warn2: Such an archive is a secret: do not publish it or hand it to strangers.
